notes: \cpara{Opens a fable: a tribe on the move, and rain that no one can explain.}
\cpara{The wise man, asked for the first time, makes up an answer: the sky spirits battle and their blood falls as rain.}

\cpara{The dialogue ends the way the one that opens ``Semantic Stopsigns'' (24 August 2007, nine days earlier) ends: a chain of questions about where each thing came from stops at a mythic origin. There the last answer is ``Never ask that question''; here it is a whisper about ``the long long ago.''}

\cpara{Names the three responses. Ignore is not asking; Explain is trying to devise an explanation; Worship is to ``enjoy the sensation of mysteriousness.'' The last takes up a line from ``Mysterious Answers to Mysterious Questions'' (25 August 2007): ``To worship a phenomenon because it seems so wonderfully mysterious is to worship your own ignorance.''}
\cpara{States the problem: every explanation raises the same three-way choice again, so hitting Explain looks like ``a road that has no end.''}

\cpara{Runs the chain from life to chemistry, atoms, nuclei, quarks and the Big Bang. At the last step the question changes, from what a thing is made of to how it got there. Both kinds of question lead to further questions, so the point stands.}
\cpara{Takes the chain to its limit: if we go on long enough, ``we must come to'' an ``Explanation That Needs No Explanation,'' and this, ``maybe,'' is ``the only explanation worth knowing.''}

\cpara{The turn: the reasoning just given was Worship. The post does not say which part earns the label. The previous paragraph makes a claim, that the chain ``must'' end somewhere, and adds a valuation, that the end is ``maybe'' ``the only explanation worth knowing.'' The claim is the old question of a first cause, which ``Semantic Stopsigns'' called ``the seeming paradox of the First Cause.'' The definition of Worship, to ``enjoy the sensation of mysteriousness,'' fits the capitals and the valuation. A reader cannot tell whether concluding that the chain ends is itself Worship, or only the reverence around it.}

\cpara{Gives the Explain response to the regress: call it a paradox and wonder how it is resolved. The post stops there. ``Semantic Stopsigns'' had also set the question aside: ``My purpose here is not to discuss the seeming paradox of the First Cause.'' A reader of the sequence meets the regress twice and is given an attitude toward it both times, with no step toward an answer.}
\cpara{Counts every way of setting the question aside as Ignore, from judging it unimportant to putting it off until tomorrow.}

\cpara{The closing line leaves the choice to the reader. The post has said nothing about when setting a question aside is the wise option. The next day's post, ```Science' as Curiosity-Stopper,'' allows it: ``Prioritize, if you must.''}
